faq.question: How much faster is the G6 Split 50W than the 30W?
faq.answer: In our benchmark, a filled 10 × 10 cm logo on stainless steel takes about 3–8 minutes on the 50W, against 4–11 on the 30W. The gap widens on deep engraving and multi-pass cut-outs, where average power matters most. Gweike lists the same 7,000 mm/s line speed for every G6 Split tier, so light surface marks gain little.

faq.question: Which lenses fit the G6 Split 50W?
faq.answer: It ships with a 175 × 175 mm (6.9 in) lens. Gweike sells 110, 150, 200 and 300 mm replacement lenses at $199 each, and lists the 300 × 300 mm lens for the 50W and above. A larger field spreads the same power over a bigger spot, so deep work slows down with the 300 mm lens.

faq.question: 50W or 70W G6 Split: which suits me?
faq.answer: The 50W starts at $3,899 with manual lift on Gweike's US store (October 2026); the 70W starts at $4,899, about $1,000 more. Choose the 50W for a mix of marking and occasional deep work. The 70W makes sense when deep engraving or cut-outs are a daily task and shorter cycles translate into money.

standoutFeatures.title: Compatible with the 300 × 300 mm lens
standoutFeatures.body: Gweike lists its 11.8 in (300 mm) replacement lens for the G6 50W and above. Useful for large plaques, panels and fixture plates holding many parts in one job.

standoutFeatures.title: Middle ground for mixed work
standoutFeatures.body: Fast enough for deeper logos and thin cut-outs, at about $1,000 less than the next tier. A sensible choice when marking is the daily job and depth is occasional.

editorialDepth.advantages: Gweike G6 Split 50W fits shops that mark stainless, aluminum, and tools daily without a CO₂ bay. A solid bench option for jewelry, tags, and small batches.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if wood, leather, or cast acrylic pay your bills. Deep metal cutting and large industrial panels often need more fiber headroom (70W or 100W) or a different machine class.
